_purpose: independently verify docs/data/glyph_map.json, because tools/encode_text.py's own docstring warns that its `roundtrip` check CANNOT do so: it builds both directions from the same map, so any self-consistent but wrong map passes (demonstrated there by rotating glyphs 500-599 by one -- story text visibly broke, yet 35/35 resources still round-tripped)
_method: compare glyph_map's output against two sources that do not derive from it: (a) the 16x16 1bpp font bitmaps in FDOTHER.DAT resource 4, rendered and read directly, and (b) text this project read off the live game screen on 2026-09-07

result_character_names.note: first pass showed 31/32 with id 28 disputed: glyph_map said 達克塞, my transcription from the small rendered image said 逢克塞. Re-rendering that glyph at 8x settles it as 達 -- glyph_map was right and my transcription was wrong. Evidence: docs/figures/glyphmap-id28-zoom-da-not-feng.png. docs/data/fdtxt000_name_table.json corrected.

observed: 索爾死亡米亞斯多德死亡
result_sample_strings.assessment: all read as coherent, contextually correct Chinese (weapons, items, dialogue, spells, shop, chapter, defeat conditions)
live_cross_checks: 風妖精 appears in Sol's spell list read live off the battle screen
道具店 is a town location label read live off the camp screen

conclusion: glyph_map agrees with the font bitmaps and with live on-screen text on every one of the 104 glyphs actually exercised, with zero mismatches once my own transcription error is removed. This is a real independent check, unlike roundtrip. It does NOT cover the remaining 94.3% of entries -- widening it means exercising more strings, not re-running roundtrip.
